title: Business Organization & Environment Adventure 2: SWOT & PESTLE
welcome_lead: Today you'll scan the internal position with SWOT and the external world with PESTLE.

concepts.def: Political, Economic, Social, Tech, Legal, Environ.
Internal negative: high debt, weak skills
External positive: new market, tech change

walkthroughs.body_html:
SWOT divides factors by origin and impact.

Internal: Strengths (S) and Weaknesses (W) — things the firm controls (resources, skills, brand).

External: Opportunities (O) and Threats (T) — things the firm reacts to (markets, rivals, laws).

SWOT is a snapshot — quick to draw but easily descriptive rather than analytical.

PESTLE breaks the external world into six forces:

Political (tax policy, stability), Economic (GDP growth, interest rates), Social (demographics, lifestyles), Technological (AI, automation), Legal (employment law, competition law), Environmental (carbon rules, climate risk).

PESTLE feeds the O and T of SWOT.

A clothing retailer faces:

- Social: rise of fast fashion → Opportunity.
- Environmental: anti-waste laws → Threat.
- Strength: strong online platform.
- Weakness: outdated stores.

SWOT prompts strategy; PESTLE keeps it grounded in macro reality.
